data.turoyo: <...> kmanṭən u tanakči, kqoyəṣ tanagaye lu goran du femawo, kmalḥamla <...>
data.translation: <...> sie holen den Klempner, der schneidet ein Stück Blech entsprechend dieser Öffnung und verlötet es <...>

rationale: First III Infectum: literal soldering with named tinsmith and object suffix, complementing the inherited magical reattachment.

summary: III has an acting tinsmith and a feminine suffixal object interpreted as the cover or sheet at a can opening. The material involved is sheet metal, and the operation preserves cheese.
I has an inanimate horn fitting around a snake, with the enclosed participant marked by ʕal-. This is the inherited attachment/enclosure meaning, without an agentive causative.
Keep kmalḥamla separate from the earlier salt-related kəmmalḥila and məloḥo in the same verse. The tinsmith context disambiguates lḥm.
No new sense, Detransitive form or fixed idiom is supported.
Confirm the exact antecedent of -la in kmalḥamla: the sheet cover or the tin container. The soldering meaning and III Infectum classification are secure.
The inherited magical reattachment of legs and the new literal soldering of a cover both fit löten, anheften; no new technical sense is necessary.
